title: Report gating rulebook and SLO contracts for enterprise ad-hoc export requests
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of ad-hoc reporting and export requests (usage snapshots, cost breakdowns, row-level exports, custom dashboards). Current intake is manual and inconsistent: requests miss key evidence, SLAs are vague, delivery lanes are not formalized and finance lacks a reproducible cost model. This leads to unpredictable delivery times, surprise engineering effort, and disputes on effort/cost for concierge deliveries.

Goal: Create a single, prescriptive 'Report Gating Rulebook' and associated SLO contracts that standardize: 1) intake evidence required from customers, 2) automated vs concierge routing logic, 3) clear delivery lanes with SLOs and chargeback guidance, and 4) data contract / retention / audit statements for legal/compliance. Deliverables include a rulebook Confluence doc, intake UI spec, classifier prototype to distinguish self-serve vs concierge requests, and cost attribution guidance for Finance.

Scope: Enterprise ad-hoc (non-bug) requests submitted via Console request flow, Support tickets flagged as 'Reporting', and direct AE/CS escalations. Excludes scheduled recurring reports that already have templates (these will be covered separately).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Rulebook doc published in Confluence with: intake evidence checklist, explicit delivery lanes (Self-serve / Scheduled / Concierge), and per-lane SLOs.
2) Intake UI spec and copy uploaded to Drive with tooltip text and evidence collection flows.
3) Prototype classifier (ENG-48211) integrated into intake flow that matches >= 80% of historical decisions on a 1k-sample test.
4) Cost attribution model agreed with Finance: per-export cost floor and optional chargeback path described.
5) Legal review completed with mandatory data retention & audit language incorporated.
6) Rollout plan with feature flags and telemetry (accept/decline rates, time-to-delivery) documented.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in average time-to-first-response for ad-hoc exports from current baseline to <=24 hours for Self-serve lane.
- >= 60% of incoming ad-hoc requests auto-routed to Self-serve or Scheduled after classifier rollout.
- Finance acceptance: modeled per-export cost estimate within 10% of measured engineering hours for first quarter.
- Decrease in disputed chargebacks by 80% after chargeback rubric publication.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Classifier misroutings could push high-effort requests into self-serve causing failures. Mitigation: conservative initial threshold, human-in-loop approval for edge cases, telemetry to quickly detect misroutes.
Risk: Legal asks delay rollout due to new retention clauses. Mitigation: ship gated 'non-sensitive' lane first and parallelize Legal review for concierge lane.
Risk: Engineering capacity constrained by rate-limiter work (ENG-50321). Mitigation: schedule dependency explicitly in rollout and offer manual concierge backlog triage until rate-limiter ships.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Beta, 2 weeks): Publish rulebook, UI mocks, and enable classifier in read-only mode (suggestions shown to triage team). Collect telemetry.
Phase 2 (Limited rollout, 3 weeks): Enable automated routing for low-risk tenants (pilot accounts), enable self-serve export templates, and surface cost-estimate badge in Console.
Phase 3 (General availability): Open automated routing broadly, enable chargeback workflow, and deprecate manual freeform intake. Monitor metrics and iterate.
Fallback: Manual concierge queue and SLA-backed expedited path for high-impact customers.
